**The homage that is two-resting, and who is worthy to make it**

text: dyczkowski mode the homage that is two resting and who is worthy to make it the work opens with a prostration and abhinavagupta takes care to say what that prostration is it is not a bending of the body nor an empty sound it is a two resting homage it rests at once in the lord whom it exalts and in the devotee whom it subordinates the words of homage jaya victory namah i bow i worship all move by one of these two directions but each must culminate in the other the victory of the lord to be real requires the devotee s self subordination the i bow of the devotee to be real must rest in the lord s excess the two the exalting and the subordinating are one act two aspects made manifest by the single word of homage before the whole assembly and the attaining of the lord the commentary tells us is the attainment of dasya of servant ness and the servant ness is extremely hard to get that is what kathamcit in some way means it is not a title it is the very heart of the eligibility and it is fruitful of the greatest good for in becoming the servant of the lord one attains the lord s own excess and all the fortunes dasyalaksmi follow from that servant ness granted by the lord s grace it is this that makes the devotee one who has attained all the homage moreover is made in the mind and the speech the mind awareness and the word essence never in the inert body even by speech the text says and by the even we understand and by the body but the prostration proper is the offering of the undivided mind and speech which is the consciousness power itself and in offering that the devotee offers the whole world to the lord as the teaching says he should offer his own self the physical prostration the bowing the eight limbed salutation is only the upacara the visible mark by which the inner offering is inferred not the primary act and so the question of who is worthy the objection arises the eligibility suits the explainer who has attained but how does it suit the mere listeners abhinavagupta s answer is that the listener and the explainer are not two separate undertakings the recognition is one and the servant ness is one it is by this that the lord s favor is won the recognition is preceded by and inferred from the lord s favor and this is where the gita s four kinds of devotees come in the distressed the seeker of knowledge the seeker of wealth and the knower all of them in their several gradations are worthy of the servant ness and of the recognition the door is not narrow in the way of the world s ranks it is narrow only in the way of the heart for what is required is the self subordination the dasya and that once attained draws the lord near preserved the right teacher samyagvyutpadaka the buddhists as makers and haters the kathamukhatilaka the unprecedented prostration the two resting homage jaya self subordination namah lord s excess the jar shines and sees kathamcit the dasya is hard to get mahaphala the attainment of all fortunes dasyalaksmi by the lord s grace vacapi by body too the homage in mind speech not the inert body the offering of the whole world he should offer his own self the physical prostration as the upacara inferred mark the satyam obstacle removal vs the greater purpose adyapi un broken by the book the explainer honored the recognition preceded by the lord s favor the listener not separate objection and answer the four gita devotees all eligible added supplied recoverable it is not a title it is the very heart of the eligibility states the dasya in offering that the devotee offers the whole world glosses the visvarpana the door is narrow only in the way of the heart the eligibility s point interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the kathamukhatilaka reference the exact gradation of the four devotees the text s continuation logged not invented

**The self is the Lord: what the recognition does**

The kārikā declares that the self alone is the Lord. And at once a sharp objection arises. A valid
means of knowledge, it is said, establishes what
text: dyczkowski mode the self is the lord what the recognition does the karika declares that the self alone is the lord and at once a sharp objection arises a valid means of knowledge it is said establishes what was not established before it serves the practical dealings of the world but the lord self on our own showing is already established so what could a pramana possibly do here what is there left for it to prove abhinavagupta s answer turns this objection around for an inert object even an established one the pramana does indeed make a new attainment it brings out some part that was not yet grasped at least the manifestation and the designation prakhya and upakhya of the thing in our dealing with it but in the self the lord there is nothing un attained to be established the manifestation and the designation are already there without them not even a trace of a thing could be known at all so the pramana here is not establishing something new what then is it doing it is foregrounding what is already present but hidden the recognition pratyabhijna does not bring the lord into being it brings the lord who was always near and always present into the foreground of our own awareness as abhinavagupta says what is hidden and standing close by is shown as primary by the coming together of the heart the recognition makes the manifestation and the designation of the self as lord no longer an instrument lost among the things of the body and the world but the primary thing that we see it is the turning of the attention the see see upon what was always before us and this recognition is the very content of the whole teaching after the upoddhata the opening the whole sastra that is to come has as its to be said content the recognition which is the jnana kriya the knowledge and action power made firm by the conviction drdhaniscaya that arises from it the two powers knowledge and action are determined at length throughout the work and the firm conviction in the self as lord is their fruit so the point is this the self is the lord and he is already established not to be newly proved but to be recognized the pramana does not reach out to a distant un known thing it turns the light of attention upon the one who was always the knower and the known the one standing near in the very act of knowing the recognition is not the acquisition of something new it is the foregrounding of the self the lord who was never absent and this the firm conviction in the self as lord is what the whole teaching sets before us preserved the coming verses 3 22 the kala drstatva grammar the pratyabhijna as the content jnana kriya the drdhaniscaya added supplied recoverable it turns the light of attention upon the one who was always the knower restates the transformation of matter the vaisesika makes it a quality of the self joined to the object by a mysterious relation called inherence samavaya abhinavagupta cuts through all of this with a single image infinite division of knowers the same body could be dealt with at once as fire and water as contradictory things in a single moment which is absurd the enjoyment is real but real as this union of **"Thence the agent too is constructed"**

The Buddhist's attack has been relentless. He has denied the self, denied the cognition, denied the
action. Now he completes it. For what holds all these together — the *relatio
text: thence the agent too is constructed the buddhist s attack has been relentless he has denied the self denied the cognition denied the action now he completes it for what holds all these together the relation between the knower and the known between the agent and the act is itself impossible and once the relation is gone thence the agent too is constructed the agent like everything else is only a fabrication a convenient construction with nothing real behind it the karika s thence gathers a fourfold absence as its reason the absence of the action the absence of the object the absence of the relation and the absence of any determination of being in any of them and the relation s absence is argued on its own terms a relation would have to stand in both its terms in the knower and the known at once but the two resting thing cannot be one what stands in two cannot be a single thing any more than the two jars in the two houses are one jar moreover the established does not expect another a thing already complete does not reach out for a relation and the dependence that a relation would impose is itself unfitting so the relation is absent and with it the agent that the relation would bind together is only constructed abhinavagupta pauses to make one methodological point and it is important the buddhist thinks he refutes the relation by a bare non perception i do not see it so it is not but a bare non perception proves non being only within a restriction of place and time here now there is no jar it cannot reach the universal non being of the relation to do that one must show a real contradiction in the opponent s own account that the very form he ascribes to the relation is contradicted by another form he ascribes to it that is a refutation grounded in the thing itself prameya nistha not a mere failure to perceive and this is where the purvapaksa the no self attack comes to its close the buddhist has shown to his own satisfaction that the self the cognition the action and the relation all fall and thence the agent too is constructed the whole edifice of a real knower and doer is for him a fabrication

**The self-luminous cognition: how memory reaches the past, and the yogin reaches the other**

Two puzzles press on the account of memory. The first is the pastness of
text: from pilot v2b argument map md dyczkowski mode the self luminous cognition how memory reaches the past and the yogin reaches the other two puzzles press on the account of memory the first is the pastness of the past we remember what happened yesterday but how if the manifestation of consciousness has no touch of time at all the answer is that the pastness is not a real quality of the object it is the being previously manifested the one light contracting under the limiting conditions of place and time yesterday thirsty with that friend i saw this jar un ripe appears as the past the manifestation is cut by these upadhis and what we call the maya word the realm of ordinary experience is precisely this contraction of the light by the conditions the memory is the re apprehension of what was previously manifested and the cognition of the object so cut by the past experience is itself a fresh act of experience there is nothing ghostly in memory it is the one light narrowed to a past moment shining again the second puzzle is the yogin s perception of another s mind the yogin is the one who has attained unity with the supreme knower for him all objects are un cut by time present in his own self as i or as i this how then does one particular appearance arise for him and with its past time specificity here abhinavagupta gives the key time is the order of appearing and not appearing the body flashing and fading moment by moment is what gives the endless difference of time those who take the body as the knower are bound in the chain of time and can never see past or future but the yogin by the teaching and the sustained meditation thins the body and then the other s cognition shines in its own place and this leads to the deepest point the nature of cognition itself the cognition is self cognition svasamvitti its own nature that which never deviates the marker neither over nor under pervading is to be self luminous the own awareness that distinguishes it utterly from the inert the jar is not self aware it is only what it is but cognition in its very being is aware of itself and precisely because it is self cognition it is also free to manifest the other the same luminous awareness that knows itself can in its freedom shine upon another s cognition the inert cannot do this only the self luminous awareness can so the yogin s knowledge of another is nothing other than the other s own cognition self luminous which the yogin by the purity and the un opposed spreading of his own cognition comes to know the upshot is a single elegant thesis cognition is self cognition it is the own awareness that is the very nature of consciousness distinguishing it from the inert and because it is self cognition it is also other manifesting it can reach the past in memory and reach the other in the yogin s perception memory and clairvoyance are not exceptions to the nature of cognition they are the overflow of the one self luminous awareness which being aware of itself is free to be aware of all preserved memory s pastness as the being previously manifested the manifestation contracted by the upadhis place yesterday thirst friend the maya word as the contraction the memory s object as a fresh experience the yogin ma vi 4 4 and the un cut objects as i i this time as the appearing not appearing order the body flashing fading giving time difference those bound by the body unable to see past future the yogin s thinning of the body the cognition as self cognition svasamvitti the own nature as the never deviating marker the self luminous distinction from the inert the self cognition manifesting the other parapi asya samvit the yogin s purity and un opposed spreading added supplied recoverable narrowed to a past moment shining again glosses the memory s contraction the overflow of the one self luminous awareness states the thesis interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the avicaritapata sankita pratibhana un investigated flash crux the kakaksivat textual joining logged not invented verdict understood and readable v2 b argues cleanly that memory reaches the past by the contraction of the one light the yogin reaches the other by the self cognition s freedom and the whole rests on the thesis that cognition is self cognition self luminous distinguishing it from the inert and free to manifest both self and other

text: dyczkowski mode the self luminous cognition is never the object of another we have seen that the yogin by the purity and the un opposed spreading of his cognition knows another s cognition but this draws a sharp objection from the epistemologist even granting that he says a cognition can never be the object of another cognition for how can one awareness be known by a second the two would have to stand in the relation of object and holder and between two cognitions no such relation is possible abhinavagupta takes this seriously and analyzes what being an object really means a thing is an object of a cognition when the awareness assimilates its form when it takes on the form of the thing as the blue awareness takes on the blue this assimilation is the sarupya the conformity of the cognition to its object and it requires that the object be both like and unlike the cognition in total identity the thing would be the cognition itself and in total difference there would be nothing to assimilate now here is the crux a cognition has no such difference from another cognition the difference of place time and form is absent between two awarenesses the difference that comes from the object the blue is not the param essence of the cognition and though the object part the blue or the intent part the passion can be an object by a separate manifestation the awareness part itself can never be an object at all an awareness cannot be spread before itself as a thing to be grasped abhinavagupta makes this vivid with two mirrors two mirrors can reflect one another each bearing the other s image because their forms being of place and time are genuinely distinct but two cognitions are not like that their form is not the place time form of things it is the self luminous awareness which has nothing in it to be set over against another awareness so the object holder relation between two cognitions is impossible there is no perception of any real difference between them this is the epistemologist s own anupalabdhi turned against him and what of maya does it not cover the awareness and make it an object no maya does not really cover the awareness s own form any more than a covering hides the burning power of the fire and even what we call a covering is in truth the producing of a form distinct from the prior state the awareness is not hidden by the world it is the world that appears in the awareness the upshot is decisive the cognition is self luminous it is never made the object of another cognition because to be an object is to be assimilated by an awareness and one awareness cannot assimilate another without the real difference that awarenesses lack the knower in other words is fundamentally conscious the ajada the not inert a self luminous presence that is never itself turned into a thing this is the establishment of the conscious knower with which the vimarsa on memory and the whole ajadapramatrsiddhi comes to its close preserved the yogin s knowledge of the other purity un opposed spreading the objection no object holder relation between cognitions the sarupya as the assimilation of the object s form the object ness requiring both difference and non difference the absence of difference between two cognitions the object part intent part as objects but the awareness part never the two mirror point the vyapakanupalabdhi dharmakirti s non perception maya not covering the awareness the fire s burning power the covering as producing a distinct form the cognition never known by another the establishment of the ajada pramatr added supplied recoverable as the blue awareness takes on the blue glosses sarupya the epistemologist s own anupalabdhi turned against him states the reversal an awareness cannot be spread before itself as a thing to be grasped the bodhamsa point interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the bamboo pillar and jar with itself examples the exact vyapaka anupalabdhi mechanics logged not invented verdict understood and readable v2 c argues cleanly that cognition is self luminous and never the object of another cognition because object ness is the assimilation of a form which requires a real difference that awarenesses lack and this establishes the conscious not inert knower the smrtisaktivimarsa and the ajadapramatrsiddhi close on this

text: pilot v2d argument map md dyczkowski mode the knowledge power manifestation as the very form of things we have examined memory and the construction but both presuppose something deeper the knowledge power jnanasakti the capacity by which anything at all is known and here abhinavagupta makes the central claim of this vimarsa the manifestation is the very form of the objects the things of the world are not hidden realities that a light shines upon from outside their being is their being manifested to know a thing is not to touch something beyond the light it is to be the light in which that thing appears consider the present beings as they manifest they manifest as the outer self the inner standing alone of consciousness pouring itself out as the external world the jar before you is not a thing outside that your mind then copies it is the inner light standing as the outer form memory and the construction for their part do not present a common object as something separate and distinct and even in perception the object does not exceed the experience that reveals it the thing is not more than its being manifested now the vijnanavadin the buddhist idealist agrees that the object is not outside but he draws the wrong conclusion he concludes that there is no object at all only the inner cognition with its blue form abhinavagupta replies that this does not follow the cognition s inner blue form is a reflection and a reflection expects a ground that it reflects as a mirror image expects the thing before the mirror so the inner blue form being a reflection points to an identical ground that produces it this is the inference of the object not as a thing hidden beyond all experience but as the ground whose reflection the blue form is even as the sense organ is inferred from the perception it causes so the object is inferred as the cause of its manifestation the object is real but its reality is to be the ground of the manifestation not a bare thing beyond it and this is the deep point the objects necessarily inhere in the consciousness self by the very re recollection paramarsa through which they are known and the essence of the manifestation the knowledge power is the reflexive awareness vimarsa the light is not a passive mirror it is the self aware light that in knowing the object knows itself the known is not something set over against the knower the knowledge re recollection is itself the known the pure never abandoning the knower being even in the un constructed perception the life is the reflexive awareness so the knowledge power is not the capacity to reach some hidden thing it is the self luminous self aware manifestation that is the very being of the world the upshot the jnanasakti is the manifestation that constitutes the objects the world is not lit from without it is the light the object is not a fiction nor a thing beyond the light but the ground that the manifestation reflects and the essence of that manifestation is the reflexive awareness the light that knows itself in knowing all this is the knowledge power the first and deepest of the powers of consciousness preserved the mangala the 21 verse plan the thesis manifestation as the object s form the present beings manifesting as the outer self memory construction without a separate common object the object not exceeding the experience the vijnanavadin answered the reflection expects a ground the inference of the object like the sense organ the objects inhering in the consciousness self by the paramarsa the reflexive awareness as the essence the knowledge re recollection as the known the reflexive awareness as the life even in the un constructed the jnana jnatr division and establishment added supplied recoverable pouring itself out as the external world glosses bahiratmana a mirror image expects the thing before the mirror states the arpaka reflection inference the light that knows itself in knowing all restates the vimarsa as the essence interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the precise bahiratmana reading the full dharmakirti dharmottara inference mechanics logged not invented verdict understood and readable v2 d argues cleanly that the knowledge power is the manifestation which is the very form of the objects the object is not beyond the light nor a fiction but the ground the manifestation reflects and the essence of the light is the reflexive awareness the self knowing that is the being of the world

speech from his uttered words and gestures one can infer what is going on in his mind the other stream abhinavagupta shows this inference cannot work and he does it with a precise analogy suppose you want to infer the fire in the sandalwood from the smoke if you set aside the sandalwood s fragrance the very thing that marks this smoke as coming from sandalwood then you establish only fire in general not the sandalwood fire the distinction must be accepted without it the desired conclusion is not reached but to infer another s mind you would need exactly such a further distinction the being gone to the other the fact that this utterance belongs to maitra and not to you and that distinction cannot be inferred from the mere utterance the utterance could belong to anything nothing in it by itself says this is maitra s intent this is another s mind and the being gone to the other abhinavagupta argues is not like the sandalwood fragrance a further distinguishing mark resting apart from the thing it is a different kind of thing entirely to press the point he notes that if every additional feature were a further distinction then cow and speckled would both be separate things and the statement the cow is the speckled would fail but that statement holds so a real further distinction is something that rests apart from the thing and the being gone to the other does not rest apart from the mere utterance in the way that would make it inferable moreover and this is the decisive point only the aimed action samihita is the wish s effect a wish produces the action it intends not a mere utterance or gesture that could be aimed at anything so from maitra s mere utterance one cannot infer his wish since the utterance does not reveal which aim it serves if the mere utterance appearances do not reach another s mind and this paves the way for karika 6 the appearances alone suffice for the dealings of the world we do not need a hidden external object behind the appearances text: from pilot v2h argument map md dyczkowski mode the light that knows itself the heart of the doctrine here in the deepest part of the vimarsa on the knowledge power abhinavagupta states the heart of the whole teaching the manifestation prakasa is not a passive inert light its very nature is the reflexive awareness vimarsa the light s own grasp of itself without the vimarsa the manifestation would be like crystal it would show the world but it would not know that it showed it it would be inert what makes the light light what makes it consciousness and not a thing is that it is aware of itself in the very act of manifesting consider the very first surge of knowing in the inner speech the middle self before the mind has split the knower from the known in the pasyanti the seeing the first stirring of the will the knower and the known are not yet two not even by their common form no distinction has yet flashed and this abhinavagupta says shines by itself it is the pure reflexive awareness before any division the proof that this is so is drawn from the swiftest of our acts in quick reading in rapid motion in hurried speech we go from line to line from place to place abandoning some things and seizing others all without pausing to reflect yet these abandonments and attainments are as we see always preceded by a re reflection paramarsa they infer their cause the re reflection and that re reflection cannot be only by the difference of knower and known for then the very swiftness of the act would fail tangled in the lineage of speech mind motion convention memory the swift act shows that the knower and the known the abandoning and the attaining are not two separate things they are one act of the self aware consciousness what is and is not separate must be non separate there is no third class to hold them apart and this is the will the first surge the first tuti the bursting as the sivadrsti says when the consciousness dharma in its splendor and joy unfolds into the varied creation and becomes the un lidded awareness that is the will s first surge and she is seen in the sudden moments in the heart at the time of remembering an effect at the moment of rapture or emotion at the sight of the beloved at the un reflected glance at the very emission of the utterance in the reading and the running in all these occasions the all power liveliness of the consciousness flashes it is the reflexive awareness the self grasping of the light seen most clearly where the mind does not pause to divide so the reflexive awareness is not a thing not an added quality it is the manifestation s own nature the light that shines is the light that knows itself and this self knowing is the para vak the supreme speech from which all the lower levels of speech the madhyama the vaikhari descend it is the lord s freedom svatantrya and his lordship aisvarya this is what abhinavagupta will draw out in the next karikas that consciousness is at once the awareness its action and its agency karika 12 and that this reflexive awareness the para vak arising by its own savor is the supreme freedom of the supreme self karika 13 the heart of the doctrine is here the light knows itself and that self knowing is the lord preserved the vimarsa as the manifestation s own nature else inert like crystal the pasyanti middle self the will surge the pramatr prameya not yet two the self shining the swift action proof quick reading motion speech the abandonment attainment the re reflection as the inferred cause the re reflection not only by difference the apohe the karya hetu and svabhava hetu no third class the sivadrsti 1 8 the iccha as the first tuti the occasions the heart the effect memory the rapture the beloved the un reflected sight the visarga the utterance the reading running the all power liveliness the para vak the freedom and lordship the madhyama vaikhari descent karika 12 citkriya citikartrta karika 13 the para vak as the aisvarya added supplied recoverable the light s own grasp of itself glosses vimarsa the swift act shows that the knower and the known are one act of the self aware consciousness the swift action proof seen most clearly where manifestation now the vimarsa on the knowledge power closes by drawing out two consequences one about words one about order first the word when we say this jar the this seems to be a thing that the word jar is pasted onto but abhinavagupta shows this is a mistake the jar word in the determination does not stand apart as a free thing that the this points at it is superimposed on the meaning and meaning is not a distinction of two things but a superimposition adhyasa and this brings us to the word s own nature if the manifested were not re recollected its being manifested itself would be impossible as the external blue being manifested is re recollected as blue so the word which is itself a manifestation necessarily has the reflexive awareness there is no further word general or specific by which it would be recalled as the blue speaker and to call it by another similar word would run into the infinite regress destroying the blue re recollection and so the blue manifestation itself hence the own form re recollection is the very nature of the meaning and because the blue word is the re collector its being able to re collect itself and the other is its self luminousness cognition shining by itself by that very shining makes the object shine it is clearly self and other manifesting so the lamp is self and other light the word is self and other re recollection second verses one to reject the prior view karika 1 one to distinguish ordered un ordered karika 2 three on the nature of order karikas 3 5 two on the division of the sphere of ordered un ordered karikas 6 7 and one karika 8 concluding that even after dividing the sphere both truly rest in the one alone then karika 9 on the creation power hence although it was said that the action of the one is not ordered the one and the rest that is rejected by the establishing of that one as the agent the buddhist holds that only momentary cognitions flash forth in a stream with no underlying owner asraya memory is just impression and if cognition is inert jada it cannot reveal an object but if it is conscious ajada it has no real temporal distinctions so how is the self anything other than this a distinct cognitions cannot serve ordinary dealing b memory is not from mere impression c cognition of the un contracted consciousness is its own power built contraction by the known object s tint this is what power and dharma mean the key image lines 98 103 the one can be of many natures without contradiction like a mirror darpana that bears many reflections without losing its own oneness so a thing whose essence is appearance abhasasara established as one by unimpeded recognition perception can take up seemingly contradictory forms in itself and without itself being divided manifest those ordered distinct appearances this is the action support kriyasraya the same reasoning establishes the relation sambandha too so by establishing the one agent all the objections about the action power are answered karika 2 only the worldly action is ordered from the time power lines 115 156 the ordered ness of the worldly action is from the time power it obtains but not of the eternal action of the **Action, time and sequence: the timeless that manifests order**

Having established the nature of the power of knowledge,
text: pilot v3a argument map md dyczkowski mode continuous philosophy bracketed interpolations action time and sequence the timeless that manifests order having established the nature of the power of knowledge abhinavagupta now turns to the power of action the two must run in parallel if consciousness s power to know the world has been shown then its power to effect the world must be shown too and here he must confront a paradox that sits at the very heart of his system the lord is beyond time and sequence utterly free of order and yet the world he manifests is shot through with sequence causes before effects moments before moments place before place how can the timeless act in time he announces the answer in the opening verse of homage he bows to siva he says who though free of sequence manifests manifold sequences the whole doctrine is in that one image and the image he will use to make it work is the mirror a mirror bears countless reflections of things before it beside it in all their variety without ever ceasing to be the one undivided mirror it is not torn into pieces by what it shows so too the one consciousness whose essence is nothing but appearance can take up within itself a host of seemingly contradictory forms the ordered distinct appearances of the world without its own oneness being divided in the least this is the action support kriyasraya the one that acts is one and it is precisely because it is one and un divided that it can show sequence at all this is aimed squarely at the buddhist the buddhist had said only momentary cognitions flash forth in a stream with no owner behind them memory is nothing but impression and cognition is either inert in which case it cannot reveal an object or conscious in which case it has no real temporal distinctions so there is no self that is anything other than this flux abhinavagupta answers each point distinct cognitions cannot serve the ordinary dealings of the world a string of unrelated flashes could never get anyone to the village memory is not mere impression and cognition is the un contracted consciousness contracting itself by its own power under the tint of the known object and that self contraction is what we call a power and a dharma it is one it is conscious and it is not inert and its oneness is no more threatened by its many appearances than a mirror s is by its reflections so the first objection the action of the one is not ordered is rejected precisely by establishing that one as the agent the one can be of many natures that is not a contradiction but now a sharper objection order is essential to action the buddhist says and how could order be in the lord who is not cut through by time here abhinavagupta draws the crucial distinction it is the worldly action that is ordered consider the raising and lowering of a hand its earlier and later moments are ordered the single action that is the cause of the hand s moving from one position to another even if in itself eternal is inferred as ordered by the force of its ordered effect so the action of ordinary worldly dealing rightly rests in distinctions and is rightly called ordered what makes it so is the time power kalasakti and this time power is nothing alien it is simply the lord s own freedom the freedom that raises the distinctions of appearance and lets one thing follow another but the lord s own action is a different matter because the lord is not cut through by time his action is not cut through by time either it is eternal like the lord himself in the manifesting of the known and the knower that underlies all our knowledge and dealing the knowledge power is the capacity to reveal but the reflexive awareness power whose very self is freedom in joining and separating is in truth the action and this action though in reality free of all sequence appears ordered it takes up the delimited forms of things in order to reveal the known as if casting the shadow of the known before it it is the timeless showing time the mirror showing order while remaining one and so the paradox dissolves the worldly action is ordered by the time power which is the lord s freedom the lord s own action is eternal un cut by time and the two are not in conflict because the sequence we see is precisely the lord s timeless freedom manifesting itself as order the mirror showing many while remaining one this is the foundation on which the rest of the vimarsa the nature of time the order of place and finally the creation power will build preserved the jnanasakti kriyasakti transition the mangala s free of sequence yet showing sequence the eight verse plan the buddhist purvapaksa momentary stream memory as impression inert or conscious dilemma abhinava s three replies the mirror image karika 1 s conclusion establish the one agent answer the objections the nanu on order in the lord the hand raising lowering example the worldly action is ordered point the time power lord s freedom the lord s own action is eternal point the appears ordered to reveal the known added supplied recoverable the world is shot through with sequence frames the paradox it is precisely because it is one that it can show sequence makes the mirror s logic explicit a string of unrelated flashes could never get anyone to the village glosses distinct cognitions cannot serve dealing this time power is nothing alien it is the lord s own freedom spells out the kalasakti svatantrya identification interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the truncated a pra si 22 and idam ityasya vicchinnavimarsasya quotations fragmentary in this excerpt the precise mechanism of vedyacchaya casting the shadow of the known logged not invented verdict understood and readable the kriyadhikara opens with a clear coherent argument the timeless lord manifests sequence without division mirror the worldly action is ordered by the time power the lord s freedom and the lord s own action is eternal the mirror is the load bearing figure that carries the whole opening what then is time people point to the sun s course the flowering of the seasons heat and cold but in truth abhinavagupta insists time is order itself the vaisesika posits a time substance the samkhya identifies it with rajas the grammarians with an eternal the buddhist with the stream of momentary being but all of them in the end are describing the same thing a sequence a this after that projected outward and called time consider how we actually measure we measure gold by a fixed weight we measure the day by the sun s apparent course caitra walks for a day and the sun s own motion in turn is measured by the water clock in every case the time is nothing but the fixed difference of nature of some appearance the sun the heat the cuckoo appearing as a measured sequence and the power that makes that sequence appear that arranges appearances one after another is the lord s own power time is therefore not a substance that cuts through things it is order entering into appearance the very freedom of consciousness showing its appearances as before and after as a dream or a magician s show is arranged by the one who dreams it but is time merely difference no for then even the fingers which differ would have temporal difference what grounds order is deeper it is the being and not being of appearances what is manifest and what is not order is the difference between the spring that appears and the summer whose appearance is withheld and who withholds and reveals the lord by his own freedom svatantrya he manifests his appearances in every relation the jar on the firm iron the jar and the cloth as distinct or the two as one undivided juice and it is only when he reveals the spring as empty of the summer that order blinks into being this power to manifest and to withhold is the time power kalasakti so order and time with it is not a thing that imposes itself on the lord it is the lord s freedom showing appearances as one then another he is the stage director of the world machine who binds and releases and so divides the universe into before and after the same freedom accounts for place as well as time the variety of formed things house courtyard shop shrine garden forest gives rise to place order the extension and separation of things in space but place order belongs to many things consider by contrast the ripening fruit it is one thing yet it ripens it passes through states one after another that is time order and it belongs to the one the lord by his freedom manifests the variety of actions caitra goes the fruit ripens and so brings time order into being and note where time lives in the known not in consciousness even in a cognition time touches only the known part the object as it appears never the self awareness the pure act of knowing which is free of it here is the crucial turn order the being and not being of appearances belongs to the finite knower the one whose marker is the void thought the breath the body for his appearance is discontinuous vicchinna his shining is not his own form he is as it were inert and it is only consciousness flashing as him that lets him appear at all such a knower is always passing in and out of manifestation and so he is always in time but the supreme knower the one once shown sakrt whose manifestation is continuous and un broken never has his appearances appear and disappear for him there is no before and after time does not touch him and since it is only with reference to him that beings are in time in the end time does not touch the beings either and the same must be said of place the beings of the finite measured knower shine as occupying mutually exclusive places this jar here that body there that is the finite knower s experience of place but the immeasurable knower whose very self is manifestation full by itself has no such division his beings shine in him like himself un measured free of place order so with respect to the pure self the lord has no place order and by reference to him neither do the beings time and place the two great frameworks of the world are both in the end nothing but the lord s freedom and they bind only the measured the finite the discontinuous never the immeasurable the once shown the eternal the world abhinavagupta sums up is the consciousness dense self filled and this the whole account of time and order is the statement of that self fullness and with this he turns to what comes next the creation power nirmanasakti of the thus knowing lord the power by which the one who knows all this actually creates the world the foundation is laid the lord is one free timeless and placeless and time and place are but his freedom showing the world as order binding only the measured and the finite preserved the three rival accounts of time vaisesika samkhya grammarians buddhist all reduce to order the gold day sun water clock measuring examples time order entering appearance the fingers counter example not mere difference being non being of appearance as the ground of order the spring summer manifestation the time power freedom the stage director verse place order in many vs time order in the one the ripening fruit time in the known not the knower the finite discontinuous knower vs the once shown immeasurable the jar body mutual exclusion the upasamhara and the creation power bridge added supplied recoverable a this after that projected outward glosses krama as time time is not a substance that cuts through things states the negative the lord s freedom showing appearances as one then another ties kalasakti to svatantrya interpretive unpacking not resolved the paninian lyablopa sasthi reading of mitatmanah k7 the force of sakrtvibhatah the fragmentary karika 9 text logged not invented verdict the full v3 a opening karikas 1 9 is now understood and readable as one sustained argument the timeless placeless lord manifests time and place as his own freedom binding only the finite discontinuous knower the mirror freedom images carry the whole vimarsa

related categories which the external view cannot make fit fit fully in this view the first karika declares that the action relation universal substance direction and time cognitions are true by stability and by use as one many support the commentary explains why the action cognition that arises elsewhere than from consciousness essence is mere action appearance cut off by maya power but the action essence as object is true because the reflexive awareness resting on it is stable not uprooted by the refuter and agrees with the intended action the being in performing object action accepts time and form manifests as that very this and caitra goes is the action the reflexive awareness continuing in this is never uprooted and the village attainment is unbroken object action in the double moon consciousness by contrast the reflexive awareness is uprooted and the object is untrue by deficiency of object action use even if it causes delight or excitement the satya asatya and samvrtisatya distinction is then drawn the conventional true is nothing of the general from its truth ness while the untrue is the double moon and the like the external action too is explained by action power alone so the external view s action is already accounted for stability is the always helper object action use is the object ness the sutra meaning is brought in by joining the prior section with the other section with the action taken as example the commentary then examines whether object action doing ness is the being ness s own form marker or near marker own form ness is metaphorical branch possessing alone is tree ness a mere exclusion and the unreal does not do object action marker ness is shown not to hold the marker is the un deviability mutually otherwise over extension and under extension would result although direct manifestation cognition and construction less consciousness are not synonyms being distinct exclusions they are marker and marked by mutual non deviation the others the knowns are then taken up and the slice breaks off mid sentence

**The valid means: what establishes, and what it produces**

Abhinavagupta now turns to the heart of the relation between the known and the knower: the valid
means of cogni
text: pilot v3c argument map md dyczkowski mode the valid means what establishes and what it produces abhinavagupta now turns to the heart of the relation between the known and the knower the valid means of cognition pramana everything in the world is established through a pramana nothing is known without one so before anything else we must determine what a pramana is and what it yields in the world s ordinary usage the answer seems simple the object the external blue or the inner pleasure by whose force the cognition stands firm within its own fixed limit as this by its own form and of this form by some further qualifying feature that object is called the valid means the blue itself one might say is what makes the cognition of blue valid but a moment s reflection undoes this the object does not stand by its own power alone if it did the blue would appear to me and not to caitra it would shine the same for everyone it appears to me and so it stands by the power of another and that other cannot be inert an inert thing could no more establish an appearance than a blind man could guide a blind man so the other must be of the nature of consciousness yet mere consciousness is not enough either an undifferentiated consciousness could never set blue apart from yellow what establishes the blue is a consciousness tinted by the blue turned toward the blue shining as the blue that appearance abhasa is what sets the blue before us and the blue it establishes is a distinct blue if the blue were not distinct from consciousness then the very same consciousness being one with everything would have to be yellow too so the appearance is the shining of a distinct blue even though in the deepest sense the blue is not other than the great light of consciousness the distinction appears nonetheless now comes the grand unification this whole arising the contraction of the light by the limiting conditions the void the body the rest is one single act of the creation power and that one act is precisely the illumination of the knower the means and the known together pramatr pramana prameya as the siddhapada puts it the one light rises born of means object and knower there is not one power for knowing another for the means another for the object it is all one light one manifestation so what concretely is the pramana for us the bound knowers in the maya bound knower contracted by the body and the rest turned inward the appearance as it were made distinct faces the external object as long as it operates it is tinted by the place and time of the object changing from moment to moment a fresh rise each instant and yet it is one and the same appearance related to the one knower spanning endless time that appearance my appearance of blue is the valid means because it is what does the work of producing the cognition of blue and what is that cognition the fruit pramiti it is abhinavagupta says the very same appearance turned inward the awareness bodhatma is the cognition the fruit of the means the means and the fruit are not two separate things nor are they mere synonyms the means is the appearance facing outward of the nature of light the fruit is the same appearance facing inward of the nature of reflexive awareness contracted by the tint of the object taking the form of the word in a single thing the cause and its fruit are both discerned as in the blue light and its reflexive awareness and the proof that the fruit is the reflexive awareness is that the operation is the fruit for the instrument s first achievement is its operation and the operation is non different from the agent being operated so in the primary sense the means and the fruit are one whatever further fruit there is the purpose served the activity the attainment may be something else again hence the reflexive awareness is the fruit and by its force the awareness is the means the reflexive awareness for its part needs the word and rests in the general form appearance free of the mark of any particular place or time that is its life even the bare this says only what is present and before so far as caitra stands here now falls within the reach of words that is the path it is by the force of the thing s own marker ness like a direct perception of the speaker that one comes to rest in the specific and this is the decisive point the pramana s operation is upon the appearance and the appearance alone it does not seize the bare thing apart from all manifestation it works in and through the appearance preserved the two kinds of relation the ordinary sense of pramana object by whose force the cognition stands as this of this form the reflection that the object doesn t stand by its own power or it would appear to everyone the other must be conscious blind leading blind mere consciousness not enough must be tinted by blue the distinct blue else all would be one consciousness yellow too the one creation power illuminating knower means known the siddhapada quote the maya knower s appearance as the pramana the cognition the same appearance turned inward reflexive awareness word form means and fruit non different in the primary sense the further fruit purpose attainment may be other vimarsa fruit bodha means the word and the general form as the reflexive awareness s life the operation on appearance alone added supplied recoverable nothing is known without one glosses pramanadhina vastusiddhi the blue would appear to me and not to caitra makes the subject relativity explicit an inert thing could no more establish an appearance than a blind man could guide a blind man unpacks the andhenandha image it does not seize the bare thing apart from all manifestation states the abhasamatre conclusion in one line interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the full list of limiting upadhis sunya deha prana beyond what s stated the exact force of the pa va 3 308 citation logged not invented verdict understood and readable the pramanavimarsa opens with a clean coherent argument the pramana is the appearance of a distinct object in consciousness standing firm by its own conscious power its fruit is the reflexive awareness of that same appearance turned inward means and fruit are one in the primary sense and the means operates on appearance alone this sets up the ten karikas on per appearance operation that follow

text: dyczkowski mode how many appearances make one thing abhinavagupta had concluded that the valid means operates on the appearance alone but this raises a pressing problem the world treats things as one the jar the fire the gold if the means seizes only an appearance how can it ever reach the single thing those appearances belong to and how can many ever shifting appearances all belong to one and the same thing the answer developed across six karikas turns on the synthesizing awareness the one reflective grasp that gathers the many appearances into one take the jar at first glance it is simply one but reflect the discriminating mind divides it it divides it according to our freedom according to our wish according to the conventions we have learned looked at from one side it is long from another round from another upright it is a being a substance a jar gold a shining thing so the one jar shows many appearances what then keeps it one it is the synthesis anusandhana the reflexive awareness that is the very light by which all these appearances shine sometimes this awareness rests in the single appearance and yields the universal the jar ness that is the same in every jar sometimes it mixes this of this form and is the synthesis that joins the appearances into the one thing it is by the synthesis that the many appearances of the jar are established as one jar the appearances though divided by viewpoint wish and trained perception the smoke and sandalwood are known by a perception born of practice are nevertheless un divided by place and time they all belong here and now so the divisions are not of the thing s being somewhere at some time they are divisions of how it appears gathered by the one awareness now the subtlety of the object action when appearances mix one of them is primary and is the common locus samanadhikaranya of the others quickened by the sentence awareness this here now is the jar the appearances that have attained one own marker ness without abandoning their difference do their object actions some actions belong to the aggregate some are fixed each to each singly the important point it is the object action that makes a thing real in the world s sense and many appearances can do one object action here is the image abhinavagupta gives separate lamp lights do not of themselves light up a single dwelling but gathered in one house they do one thing they make it bright streams falling separately into the ocean with their countless waves nevertheless as a whole do one thing so the jar the gold the red the great their several appearances together produce a single object action say the great delight fit for bathing the image of siva and the doer of that one effect must be one the one cognition the one reflexive awareness is marked by the one object action and what about the fire its heat its denotation as fire here abhinavagupta draws the crucial distinction between what needs nothing else and what depends on another the heat appearance of the fire is un opposed un created fixed everywhere and always it needs no other object but the fire as fuel the fire as cause of smoke these depend on another object the fuel the smoke and the very meaning of the word fire is fixed by convention all of these the heat the denotation are the fire s own form svabhava and they are established by the one valid means the single perception that looks as it were to the glance of the determinative power niyati so even though the means seizes the appearance the thing s own form what makes the fire fire and not something else is fixed and known through the one perception the conclusion of the whole sequence the pramana operates on appearance but it does not lose the thing the one synthesizing awareness gathers the many appearances into the one thing the one object action confirms its reality and the niyati power fixes its own form the one and the many are not in conflict they are two phases of the same appearance gathered by the awareness and fixed by the power this is the distinction and non distinction doctrine applied to the valid means itself preserved the per appearance operation of the pramana the one jar divided by freedom wish convention the threefold division the synthesis anusandhana as what makes the many one the long round upright smoke sandalwood divisions the trained perception va pa 1 35 un divided by place time the being jar substance gold shining word footings the primary locus co reference samanadhikaranya the aggregate vs fixed object action the universal as the appearance mere tinging the individual the blue blue lotus vs caitra maitra co reference difference the streams in ocean and lamp lights images the one object action siva linga delight the fire s heat anapeksa vs fuel smoke vastvantarapeksa the convention fixed denotation the one perception establishing the own form the niyati power added supplied recoverable they all belong here and now glosses un divided by place time it is the object action that makes a thing real in the world s sense restates arthakriyakarita lokika vastusattva they do one thing they make it bright spells out the lamp image what makes the fire fire and not something else glosses the own form interpretive unpacking not resolved the exact force of the va pa 1 35 citation the niyati power s precise relation to kalasakti the karika 8 denotation clause logged not invented verdict understood and readable the sequence shows cleanly how the per appearance pramana still reaches the one thing by the synthesizing awareness many one the one object action confirming reality and the niyati fixed own form known through the one perception

text: dyczkowski mode causality is the conscious knower s agency in the previous vimarsa the relation between the known and the knower was shown to be the very expansion of the action power now abhinavagupta turns to the other great relation cause and effect and he announces his thesis without hesitation the essence of cause and effect is nothing but the relation of agent and object of action causality in the end is the agency of a conscious knower everything that follows eleven karikas of argument against the inert the buddhist and the samkhya serves to prove that single claim it begins with the lord this ancient knower manifests the world of beings without break how does he do it by his will the un divided un ordered will that is non different from him and where are these beings for him in his infinite power all beings are ultimately his own powers this will driven manifesting is precisely his action his making his creating the objection if the will is eternal then creation and destruction would be simultaneous if occasional then it needs another cause is answered the will is tinted by the particular thing to be made and so it is not simultaneous with everything at once now the hard work to show that the inert cannot be a cause take the seed and the sprout the inert seed cannot endow the sprout with being for the sprout is either already existent in which case nothing is acquired or non existent in which case it cannot come to be since the non existent has no nature by which to gain existence the claim that the effect is both existent and non existent or neither is self contradictory the blue cannot become yellow however hard we try so the non existent cannot acquire existence hence the inert material cause has no real causal power the real cause is elsewhere the cause abhinavagupta argues across the next karikas is the conscious the potter creates the pot by his power the yogin by his will alone brings about an effect without any clay or seed if the inert seed and clay were the true causes this would be impossible but it is not impossible which shows that the true cause is consciousness the free will that shapes the effect the whole apparatus of the inner and outer the two appearances resolves into this the effect arises from the conscious knower s will and ultimately from the lord and what of inference the way we come to know causes at all here abhinavagupta examines the own nature reason svabhavahetu it has two kinds in the first the cause effect relation is clear and embryonic it is fiery because it is smoky where fire is the cause of smoke in the second the relation is reversed take the famous example the simsapa a kind of tree from this is a simsapa we infer this is a tree but here there is no otherness the simsapa ness is not a separate thing from the tree ness it is the tree ness in a specific form so the entailment holds wherever the simsapa ness is the tree ness is even though the genuine causal relation that requires two distinct things is absent this is the basis of all inference the cause is necessarily present with the effect fixed by the determinative power and the simsapa born from its own seed by the rule that a thing arises from its own full complement of causes is precisely the simsapa ness that excludes non tree ness the upshot causality even at the level of inference is grounded in a real necessary relation not in the power of the inert the buddhist s and the samkhya s accounts of causality far from threatening this actually rest on the same basis when understood rightly and this entire edifice shows that the agency of the knower which is the essence of causality is not something that could belong to a limited non lordship being it requires the lord causality in the end is the lord s will at work the relation of agent and object of action expanded through the whole world preserved the mangala the 21 verse plan thesis 1 reject inert 3 conscious agent 6 anumana niyati 3 sakya 3 kapila 3 non lordship 2 karika 1 lord manifests by will beings are his powers 1 5 10 the eternal occasional will objection and its answer the satkaryavada existent non clear embryonic fire smoke reversed simsapa tree the non otherness of simsapa ness and tree ness the cause fixed to the effect by the niyati power the ekasamagri rule the co opting of the buddhist and **Inference across knowers, and the mirror of consciousness**

We have said that causality is the conscious knower's agency. But this draws a sharp objection from
the Buddh
text: pilot v3h argument map md dyczkowski mode inference across knowers and the mirror of consciousness we have said that causality is the conscious knower s agency but this draws a sharp objection from the buddhist idealist the vijnanavadin if everything is appearance he says then cause and effect are only relations between appearances an un manifested fire is nothing at all so how can the smoke appearance arise from it and how can you infer the fire from the smoke abhinavagupta s answer is subtle and rests on the one creation the vijnanavadin holding each conscious stream to have its own private appearances could find cause and effect only within his own smoke and fire appearances he can never reach another s but in our view this is wrong the lord creates the appearances for all the knowers at once as one so when we grasp the pervasion that smoke implies fire the smoke appearance and the fire appearance belong in the lord s single creation to every knower alike the smoke appearance arises from the fire appearance and this pervasion can be grasped once for all and for the whole range of knowers from the worm to the omniscient the fire appearance is one not split by the difference of streams so the smoke can arise from it and from nothing else that fire appearance being indirect to the one who infers is what we call the cause of the lord adhipatipratyaya it is new not like the smoke that is born of smoke it is the non wandering effect marker by which the inference is actually made so inference holds across knowers because the lord has created the appearances as one now the dependence of cause and effect the in this existing this is that the pervasion expresses here abhinavagupta is careful the dependence is not a real otherness between two separate things the fire and its heat their distinction is only constructed the fire as the shining own marker cannot have the heat as a separate own form both are of equal cause both come from the one reality so in truth the dependence is one quickened by the synthesis by the awareness that joins them the grammatical point the locative in fire there is heat is not meaningless nor does it point to a merely fabricated referent it is real and it is supported by the one knower the dependence of cause and effect is not two things leaning on each other it is one thing known as one but what if the samkhya with its own account of transformation offers a better story here abhinavagupta shows that even the samkhya s dry cause and effect is not dry the samkhya says there is one substance the seed or the primal principle with an ordered variety of natures the earlier nature is the cause the later is the effect the whole evolves by transformation parinama but abhinavagupta s point is that the transformation itself is an action the transition from the earlier nature given up to the later nature newly unfolded is precisely the agent act object structure the freedom of transforming which is agency so even in the samkhya view causality is not the dry change of a thing it already contains the free knower s act the intellect the earth the sprout all are states of the one substance and the transformation that runs through them is an action and finally the great closing argument why only consciousness can bear difference and non difference at all the inert abhinavagupta says is a fixed form it is a known object and as a known object it is different with respect to another thing the blue as against the non blue and non different with respect to itself but the very same nature cannot be both different and non different that is a contradiction so the inert being a known object cannot be many natured but consciousness is different it does not fall into the state of a known object like a clear free mirror it bears the whole variety of appearances as its reflections pratibimba and those reflections are distinct even within the one mirror without the mirror being torn apart so difference and non difference the very structure of the world the cause in the effect the one in the many fits only in consciousness never in the inert the objection then why don t the elephant and the mountain appearing in the one conflict with its one ness is answered because they are in the mirror they do not touch the mirror s own form they are its reflections and the free mirror shows all even by its mere limpidity alone this is its might the whole vimarsa thus closes on the mirror image of consciousness the one reality that can bear the world s difference and non difference because it is a free clear light that reflects all without being divided by any reflection preserved the vijnanavadin s objection appearances only un manifested fire is nothing smoke fire impossible the lord s single creation of appearances across knowers the pervasion grasped once for all the one fire appearance across streams worm omniscient the adhipatipratyaya lord s cause the new nutana fire appearance the non wandering effect marker the in this existing this is pervasion dependence not real otherness fire heat constructed distinction synthesis quickened the locative not meaningless constructed but real one knower supported the samkhya s one substance ordered variety transformation as action agent act object freedom the states intellect earth sprout the triguna the inert as fixed form both different and non different contradiction only consciousness like a clear free mirror bears reflections the elephant mountain in the mirror the mere limpidity might added supplied recoverable he can never reach another s glosses the vijnanavadin s privacy it is one thing known as one states the synthesis dependence the transformation itself is an action the k18 crux in one line interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact four case paksacatustaya dependence enumeration in k16 the full scope of the adhipatipratyaya logged not invented verdict understood and readable the vimarsa argues cleanly that inference holds across knowers by the lord s one creation dependence is synthesis quickened not real otherness the samkhya s transformation already contains agency and only the free mirror of consciousness can bear difference and non difference

**The coverings and the categories of the known**

Descending from the pure realm, we come to the world of the bound knower. Here the pure self is not
seen as it is; it is
text: pilot v3k argument map md dyczkowski mode the coverings and the categories of the known descending from the pure realm we come to the world of the bound knower here the pure self is not seen as it is it is covered by a set of limiting sheaths the kancukas literally the armours or coverings these are niyati fixity kala time raga attachment vidya the limited knowledge and kala the limited agency in the bound state the one flavored reality is seen as divided and the self s i ness is mistakenly found in what is not the self in the body the breath the mind take the first of these niyati the fixative power in the world we say the seed is the cause of the sprout not of the pot the clay is the cause of the pot not of the sprout this apparent fixing of each effect to its own cause this is niyati but abhinavagupta s point is that this fixity which seems to be a feature of the things themselves in truth belongs to the knower not to the known in reality the lord alone shines forth as this is the cause of that the binding of each cause to its effect as it appears is a covering laid over the reality by the limited knower so too with time and with attachment the whole flux of the mind rooted in desire and envy is the raga covering these are the armours that hide the pure self in the bound state the bound knower the one whose being is measured by the void thought the breath the body is the one who knows the separated objects he is the mayiya knower the knower in the realm of maya facing outward toward the distinct things of the world and the objects he knows are the categories of the known prameya which are counted as twenty three they fall into three groups first the one pradhana the root cause the un divided matter out of which the world evolves in the samkhya manner second the thirteen organs the external and internal instruments of knowing and acting the five senses the five organs of action and the inner organ with its aspects of mind ego and intellect third the ten fold effect group the five subtle elements tanmatras and the five gross elements distinguished as subtle and gross these twenty three abhinavagupta notes are the known in the impure realm but he adds an important caveat these categories the pradhana the subtle and gross elements are not truly graspable by the common marker the ordinary perception of the world they are not sensible in the ordinary way and even their instrument ness is not fitting in the usual sense so the categories of the known in the bound realm are not things we perceive plainly they are the structure of the divided world laid out by the maya power over the one reality and so the prathamo vimarsa of the agamadhikara comes to its close it has traced the categories from the sivatattva the body of all down through the pure group and into the impure realm where the self is covered by the kancukas and the world is divided into the twenty three categories of the known all of it in the end is the one consciousness woven warp and woof hidden from the bound knower by the coverings that are themselves in truth aspects of the knower rather than of the things this sets the stage for the next vimarsa which will analyze the bound and the lord pasu and pati in their full distinction preserved the kancukas niyati kala raga vidya kala the i ness in the non self the niyati as the fixing of cause to effect seed sprout clay pot the niyati belongs to the knower not the known matrabhasanadvarena the raga as the mind flux rooted in attachment the sunyadi bound knower knowing the separated objects the twenty three fold known one pradhana thirteen organs ten fold effect the gross subtle distinction the un sensible ness of the pradhana and the un fitting instrument ness the 1 colophon added supplied recoverable the armours or coverings glosses kancuka in the bound state the one flavored reality is seen as divided states k8 this is the mayiya knower facing outward glosses the sunyadi knower interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact thirteen organ count samkhya enumeration presupposed the detail is in the vivrti the precise mechanism of karika 8 logged not invented verdict understood and readable the prathamo vimarsa of the agamadhikara closes cleanly the pure self is covered by the kancukas which belong to the knower not the known the bound knower knows the divided world and the known is the twenty three fold pradhana thirteen organs ten fold effect setting up the pasu pati analysis to come

text: pilot v3l argument map md dyczkowski mode the knowers and the stains that bind we have set out the categories of the known the world that is known but the heart of this whole teaching is the recognition of the lord in the self and to recognize him we must understand the knowers themselves for there are many knowers from the bound to the pure and they are distinguished by the stains that bind them abhinavagupta opens this vimarsa with a homage to the one who wields the trident cutting the three nooses and those three nooses are the three stains mala that will occupy him throughout the stain of finitude anava the stain of objectivity mayiya and the stain of action karma the knower states have their presiding deities in the pure state where the knower stands in his mere knower ness the objects withdrawn the presider is rudra the supreme siva who as the lord brings his worshippers into that state and who even within the realm of maya is the one with the opened third eye but in the spread of the distinct world the presiders are brahma and visnu brahma in the production of the spread visnu in its flowing continuation and the difference is this these two make the this the object primary and the i the knower essence subordinate whereas the pure rudra makes the i primary they are not third eyed as the rudra is yet even these brahma and visnu forms are not something apart from the lord they shine as the qualities of the intellect not as the pure consciousness itself their form is the lordship the freedom the knowledge the action power standing as the support of the world now the bound knower he is the one blind by maya wandering in samsara bound by his actions this is the pasu the animal the knower who has lost his freedom and over against him stands the pati the lord the knower whose own members the beings of the world are his own the bound one is bound because he has suffered the loss of freedom of the awareness he has become un aware of his own freedom and so he is caught in the objects this is the working of the maya the manifestation of the distinct known the world spread out as other than the self which gives us birth and enjoyment and which is the mayiya stain the knowers come in grades there are the pure ones those who even in the unity of the awareness marker are mutually distinct and who lack the highest agency these are the vidyesvara group there are the pralayakala the dissolved ones absorbed in the state of dissolution who have only the stain of finitude their form the un awareness of the void and the rest and even the aware ones who possess agency still stand in the stain of action indeed all the becoming ones the gods and men and the rest have the three fold stain finitude objectivity action and binding them all is the kala the limited agency which raises the consciousness essence into the narrow form of the individual agent so the picture is complete beneath the lord who is free and whole lie the many knowers bound each by his stain the finitude that shrinks the infinite self into a single soul the maya that spreads the world out as other and the action that keeps the soul bound in the round of birth and enjoyment it is these three nooses that the trident bearing lord cuts and to understand how they are cut how the bound knower can be released into the recognition of his own lordship abhinavagupta will turn next to the states and the entry the samavesa through which the bound one rises to his true nature preserved the mangala the trident the three nooses the pasatraya the 20 verse plan the presiding deities rudra in the pure state third eyed making the i primary brahma in production visnu in continuation making the this primary the brahmadi forms as buddhi qualities the aisvarya not pure consciousness the bound knower blind by maya in samsara action bound the pati the lord of the own members the freedom loss maya as the distinct known manifestation giving birth and enjoyment the grades pure ones lacking highest agency mutual distinctness the pralayakala in dissolution with the anava stain the karma stain even of the aware agents the three fold stain of all the becoming ones the kala raised consciousness essence added supplied recoverable and those three nooses are the three stains glosses the pasatraya he has become un aware of his own freedom states the svatantryahani which gives us birth and enjoyment restates the mayakhya janmabhogada interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact vidyesvara pralayakala vijnanakala enumeration the text is dense the detail is in the vivrti logged not invented verdict understood and readable the dvitiyo vimarsa lays out the knowers and the stains clearly the presiding deities of the states the bound knower and the lord the three stains finitude objectivity action that bind all the becoming ones and the kala raised agency with the release the cutting of the three nooses to follow

bond and the liberation the great question is how the bound knower relates to the lord for the bound one does not merely suffer the world he creates it after his own fashion but his creation is not the lord s the bound one s creation is un common asadharani it is private his own per knower and per moment vanishing with him yet it does not stand on its own it is sustained by the lord s creation jivanmukta who at the fall of the body is simply the supreme lord even the world of maya is in truth the manifestation of consciousness untouched by place and time even here the lord is present the
